title: [Shortcut Guide] Default "Hold Windows key" behavior interferes with Win+V and Win+H
summary: The reporter confirmed the existing Shortcut Guide settings are a practical workaround for their case, while noting the hold-key default can still be finicky for accessibility-sensitive workflows.

status.label: Needs team follow-up
status.detail: The author replied after the maintainer workaround guidance. The issue no longer needs the reporter for the same confirmation; it needs a maintainer/product decision on whether the current settings guidance is sufficient or whether defaults/discoverability should change.

next_action.label: Team response needed
next_action.reason: Do not ask the reporter to repeat the confirmation. A maintainer should decide whether to close as handled-by-settings, document the workaround, or keep the issue open for defaults/discoverability/accessibility follow-up.

judgment.rationale: The latest reporter response confirms the existing controls are usable enough for the reporter by turning Hold Windows key off and using the activation shortcut, while preserving an accessibility/discoverability concern for maintainer judgment. Because the public thread already contains maintainer guidance and the issue carries Needs-Team-Response, a dashboard request-info action would be duplicative.
evidence: The original report describes Win+V and Win+H being disrupted by the default Hold Windows key behavior.
A maintainer explained the existing controls: disable close-on-release, increase hold duration, or turn Hold Windows key off and use the activation shortcut.
The reporter replied on 2026-09-20 that turning Hold Windows key off and using the activation shortcut is probably the practical option for their use, especially with dexterity issues.
Current labels include Needs-Team-Response and Status-Reproducible, not Needs-Author-Feedback.
judgment.recommended_action: Let the PowerToys team decide whether the current settings guidance is sufficient, whether discoverability/defaults need product follow-up, or whether to close as handled by existing configuration.

fix_assessment.rationale: A code fix is not currently selected by the lightweight pass because the latest public discussion points to existing configuration options and a team/product decision rather than missing reporter evidence.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide Hold Windows key can interfere with built-in Windows shortcuts when the hold timer activates; current settings can mitigate it, but the reporter raised usability/accessibility concerns.
known_information: The report covers PowerToys 0.101.2362.0 on Windows 11 25H2.
The issue affects Shortcut Guide Hold Windows key behavior with Win+V Clipboard History and Win+H Voice typing.
Disabling Hold Windows key avoids the interference.
A maintainer identified existing controls: close-on-release, hold duration, and using the activation shortcut instead.
The reporter replied that Hold Windows key Off plus the activation shortcut is probably the practical option for their use, but users with different dexterity needs may see different tradeoffs.
inferences: The immediate reporter-actionable question has been answered.
Remaining work is a maintainer/product decision about whether settings guidance is enough or whether defaults/discoverability/accessibility should be improved.
